area: AREA 2: camera-move faults (G-MOVES distribution, G-AIM, G-ANCHOR, G-STILL, M2) — self-curing motion heads in the plan battery
summary: Root problem: the registered cure for G-MOVES|G-STILL|G-AIM, plan_cures.vary_heads (studio/plan_cures.py:131-158, dispatched at CURES line 332), can only produce two heads — PUSH ("The camera pushes in toward {aim} across the whole shot") and LOCKED — so on ep18 it drove push_slow to share 0.30 and locked to 0.26 while distinct moves stayed at 6 < MIN_MOVES 8; and "M2 shot N:" / "G-ANCHOR shot N:" fault rows match no CURES pattern, so plan_repair returns them as "creative" and they became hand edits. The mechanism: a new mechanical module studio/move_rebalance.py renders heads from the full camera catalog (8 legal move templates keyed by shot size, never tilt_down/crane_down/rack_focus), picks per shot the least-used legal move whose aim is a noun provably held by at_rest, with an amount chosen under plan_gates.cap_for and "across the whole shot" — and verifies every candidate by replaying the real gate predicates (move_id/still_fault/aimed_at+in_cell/anchored_truck/amount-vs-cap/motion_faults M2, plus prev/next move_id for twice-running) before writing it, which is the G-CROWD-CLOSE "cure measures like the checker" pattern. Shots where no mechanical candidate passes go to one targeted workhorse structured-output call (studio/move_llm.py via studio/llm.structured, guard_spend-walled, FakeModel-injectable) with a one-sentence "The camera ..." contract validated by pydantic and then re-verified by the same head_ok predicate; a head that still fails after one re-ask is returned uncured to the writer path, never looped. M2 shots get the new head PREPENDED (camera_clause proves they have no camera half), all other shots keep their subject clause and rest clauses exactly as take_ladder.substitute does.

cures.fault: G-MOVES distinct < 8 / top share > 0.25 / same move twice running (ep18 failed twice: 6 distinct, push_slow 0.30, locked 0.26)
cures.how: studio/move_rebalance.py:rebalance(doc, indices) -> (doc, unfixed). (1) build probe shots; ids = plan_gates.move_ids(probes); counts = Counter(ids). (2) rewrite set R = indices from fault rows UNION greedily-chosen carriers of the top-share id until projected share <= 0.25 UNION the later shot of each twice-running pair UNION, while len(set(ids)) < 8, further carriers of the most-common ids — skipping dialogue shots (any line in doc['lines'] with kind=='dialogue' on that shot) except to rewrite them to 'locked' only (camera_catalog: locked carries dialogue best). (3) per shot in R ascending: candidates = LEGAL[shot.size] sorted by (counts[id], catalog order); LEGAL = {wide/full: [pan_to, crane_up, pull_reveal, tilt_up, follow, track_lateral, locked], medium: [push_slow, follow, pull_reveal, tilt_up, pan_to, track_lateral, locked], medium_close: [push_slow, tilt_up, pull_reveal, locked], close: [locked, pull_reveal, push_slow], extreme_close: [locked, pull_reveal], insert: [locked, track_lateral, crane_up, pull_reveal, push_slow]} — tilt_down/crane_down/rack_focus/handheld/orbit never offered (IGNORED set + untested + one-per-episode). (4) aims from cell_aims(shot): split at_rest on [;.,], take episode_spec.head_noun of each clause, FOCUS clause first, drop NOISE words and drop any noun matching a token (>3 letters) of setup['props'] ids not already named by the shot's pre-rewrite frame+motion (keeps G-SOURCE.staged_props from acquiring a new unspanned claim). (5) amount = largest rung of the ordered ladder [hand's breadth 1.0, forearm 2.5, head's height 3.0, short stride 5.0, stride 10.0, two strides 20.0] that is <= plan_gates.cap_for(probe, setup)[0] and <= TRAVEL_PER_SECOND * projected shot seconds. (6) head = HEADS[move].format(aim/a/b/amount); HEADS = {locked: 'The camera holds a locked-off frame', push_slow: 'The camera pushes in slowly toward the {aim}, travelling {amount}, across the whole shot', pull_reveal: 'The camera pulls back from the {aim}, travelling {amount}, across the whole shot', pan_to: 'The camera pans from the {a} to the {b}, travelling {amount}, across the whole shot', tilt_up: 'The camera tilts up from the {a} to the {b}, travelling {amount}, across the whole shot', track_lateral: 'The camera tracks sideways to the right, past the {aim}, travelling {amount}, across the whole shot', follow: 'The camera tracks behind the {aim}, travelling {amount}, across the whole shot', crane_up: 'The camera rises slowly above the {aim}, travelling {amount}, across the whole shot'} — verified against plan_gates.MOVE_VERBS first-match: 'pushes'->push_slow, 'pulls'->pull_reveal, 'pans from A to B'->pan_to (and ', travelling' sits in cell_gates.ENDS' lookahead so {b} is captured cleanly), 'tracks behind'->follow, 'tracks sideways'->track_lateral, 'rises'->crane_up, 'holds' startswith MOVES 'hold' so M2 passes; SAID_AMOUNT in episode_ref_official.py (line ~745) strips ', travelling {amount}' from the take prompt, so H3 sees verb+direction only, per 'H3 obeys direction, not amount'. (7) accept the first (move, aim) where head_ok passes; splice via the take_ladder.substitute shape (take_ladder.py:279-284): new_head + '; ' + camera_clause(old_head)[1] subject half if any + untouched rest clauses. first-wins, counts updated after each accept, pure function of doc -> deterministic.

cures.fault: M2: the head names no camera move (ep18 shot 12) — row currently matches no cure and bounces to the writer
cures.how: same rebalance() path; an M2 shot is detected by ro.camera_clause(plan_gates.head_of(motion))[0] == '' (episode_ref_official.py:785), in which case ALL existing clauses are subject/action clauses and the new head is PREPENDED: new_motion = head + '; ' + old_motion — never replacing clause 0, which on an M2 shot is the first action. The chosen head follows the same LEGAL/aims/amount/head_ok machinery, so the cure simultaneously satisfies M2's own demand ('with a measured amount and across the whole shot', episode_spec.py:884), G-AIM, G-STILL and the running rule. M9/M10 rows are explicitly NOT matched by the dispatcher pattern — they accuse the subject clauses and remain the writer's.

cures.fault: no mechanical candidate passes head_ok (every legal move for the size collides with neighbours, or at_rest yields no clean aim noun)
cures.est_cost_usd: ~$0.0004 per call real (300-900 prompt tokens + ~40 output on gpt-5.6-luna at $0.20/$1.20 per M); guard_spend reserves ~$0.016 per call via EXPECTED_OUTPUT_TOKENS=13000; worst case ~24 shots x 2 asks < $0.04 real per episode against the $3.00 ceiling
cures.how: studio/move_llm.py:fallback_head(shot_doc, setup_doc, counts, prev_id, next_id) -> str | None. Tier: "workhorse" (models.yaml line 34, gpt-5.6-luna). Call: llm.structured("workhorse", prompt, MotionHead, retries=3, _agent=None) — the native structured caller (_NativeStructuredCaller, llm.py:166) runs guard_spend before the request and records spend after; _agent is the mandatory test seam. Output contract: class MotionHead(BaseModel): head: str — with a field_validator raising ValueError (which the caller surfaces as StructuredOutputException and llm.re_ask quotes back) unless: head matches ^The camera [a-z], contains no ';', is <= 30 words, and either equals the locked phrasing or contains "across the whole shot". After a schema-valid answer, run move_rebalance.head_ok on it; on failure, ONE manual re-ask built with llm.re_ask(prompt, exc) carrying the exact failed predicate names; a second failure returns None and plan_repair leaves the shot's fault row in `uncured` (writer path, exit 1) — bounded, never a loop. ContentFiltered and OverBudget propagate as uncured, never retried.

files.change: NEW (~180 lines, functions of 10-20 lines each): HEADS (8 catalog templates), LEGAL (size -> ordered move ids), AMOUNT_LADDER + amount_for(cap, seconds), cell_aims(shot, setup, pre_text), probe(shot_doc) -> SimpleNamespace, render_head(move, aims, amount), head_ok(shot, head, prev_id, next_id, setup) replaying plan_gates.move_id/still_fault/amount/cap_for + cell_gates.aimed_at/in_cell/anchored_truck + episode_spec.motion_faults M2, splice(motion, head) (prepend on empty camera_clause, else take_ladder.substitute shape), choose(shot, counts, prev_id, next_id, setup) and rebalance(doc, indices) -> (doc, unfixed). Imports plan_gates, cell_gates, episode_spec, episode_ref_official only — no llm import, stays $0 and book-neutral.

NEW (~80 lines): MotionHead pydantic model with the strict head validator; PROMPT template above; fallback_head(...) calling llm.structured("workhorse", ...) then move_rebalance.head_ok, one re_ask, None on second failure; cure_unfixed(doc, unfixed, setups) applying accepted heads via move_rebalance.splice and returning the still-unfixed indices.

risks: G-SOURCE coupling: a new head's aim noun can token-match a setup prop id and create a claim needing a chapter span (plan_gates.staged_props reads CLAIM_FIELDS including motion); mitigated in cell_aims by excluding prop-id tokens not already in the shot's pre-rewrite prose — but a false negative here surfaces as a G-SOURCE row next round, which plan_repair cannot cure (correct: it goes to the writer, not silently shipped)

regex round-trip fragility: head_ok's guarantees hold only while HEADS phrasings and plan_gates.MOVE_VERBS / cell_gates.STARTS+ENDS stay in agreement; the round-trip test (every template -> its own move_id, every aim recoverable by aimed_at) is the lock — any future catalog wording change must keep it green

plan_repair run standalone from the CLI has no spend_context, so guard_spend is a no-op there (documented llm.py behavior, 'outside an episode: no wall'); under drive.py the runner's context walls it — worst unguarded exposure is ~$0.04/episode on workhorse rates

distribution feasibility: a plan of mostly close/medium_close shots has only 3-4 legal moves per size, so MIN_MOVES=8 may be unreachable mechanically on a short plan; the llm fallback is bounded by the SAME legality table, so such a plan correctly exits 1 to the writer rather than looping — ROUNDS=6 and the 'nothing cured this round' break at plan_repair.py line 135 already prevent spin

vary_heads removal from CURES changes historical repair behavior for G-STILL-only rows; any existing test importing vary_heads still passes since the function stays, but a fixture asserting the old PUSH/LOCKED output text must be updated to the new templates

the G-MOVES gate is HARD only on new-form plans (Episode.new_form, plan_gates line ~704) — on an old-form plan the rows print as advisories, fault_rows still collects nothing for them (advisory lines are filtered at plan_repair.py fault_rows), so the cure never fires on historical plans: correct, but worth a test if old-form books return
